summary: Unexpected 429s for dedicated pool caused by corporate-proxy HTTP/2 connection pooling — duplicate quota accounting
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429 throttles for requests routed to their Dedicated pool during high-concurrency periods. Impact: production traffic (ingest + function-calling streams) receives sporadic 429s causing user-facing latency spikes and failed batches. Pattern appears during morning US-East traffic ramp and after scheduled autoscaler warmups.

Observed behavior: Multiple simultaneous requests from the customer's workers show 429s even though the token usage shown in the console is below configured tenant quota. Customer suspects token double-counting.

Expected behavior: Tenant-level quota should account correctly for concurrent connections, and identical API key traffic should not be double-counted due to proxy connection reuse.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs ~200 parallel workers in us-east with a single API key against dedicated pool; many workers use HTTP/2 keepalive via a corporate edge proxy.
2) Start a mixed workload: short streaming starts (chat) and batch embedding jobs concurrently.
3) Wait for autoscaler warmup to finish and observe token refills + quota counters in Console.
4) Notice spikes of 429 responses from the API while console reports apparent spare quota for the tenant.
5) Toggling client-side HTTP/2 connection reuse to each worker opening its own connection reduces 429s in reproduction.
logs_and_traces: Selected trace examples: edge-proxy logs show the same API key appearing on multiple simultaneous HTTP/2 streams with different upstream connection IDs. Rate-limiter logs show per-connection increment events with no session dedupe key, causing the same logical API key consumption to be recorded twice. Example trace IDs: trace-20260310-az1-1122, trace-20260310-az1-1137. Console token accounting snapshot attached in customer upload (trimmed JSON).
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: confirmed customer quota settings and that Dedicated pool had available capacity. Reproduced locally with a corp-proxy shim that multiplexes streams over pooled upstream connections. SRE ran a capture on edge-proxy: observed that our rate accounting was keyed by (upstream_connection_id, route) rather than by API key + route in the hot path for HTTP/2. When a proxy reuses upstream connections and multiplexes client logical sessions, each HTTP/2 stream produced per-connection counters that incremented the tenant bucket multiple times. This is amplified during autoscaler warmups because many short-lived streams start concurrently and health checks create transient connections that further skew counting. Hypothesis: edge-proxy was introduced with a perf change that switched to per-connection counters to avoid lock contention; this inadvertently produced duplicates when connection pooling sits in front of the proxy. Related to a 2025 change in edge-proxy metrics (#PR-512).
temporary_workaround: Ask customer to disable HTTP/2 connection pooling at the corp-proxy for their Redwood origin (force each worker to open a distinct upstream connection), or increase tenant burst credit temporarily. Support also provided a client-side recommendation: add a short randomized jitter to worker start times to avoid synchronized warmups. Both reduced observed 429s in customer testing.
resolution:
Engineering change in progress: patch edge-proxy to include API-key session deduplication in the rate accounting hot path and fall back to a shared atomic counter keyed by (api_key, route, logical_session_id) when available. PR created to revert the per-connection-only counter optimization and add tests that simulate HTTP/2 connection pooling. Target deploy to staging on 2026-03-15 and rollout to us-east on 2026-03-17 behind a gradual canary. Once patch is deployed, ask customer to revert the temporary proxy config.

Post-deploy follow-ups: add a unit test for multiplexed upstreams, update runbook to document proxy-interaction symptoms, and add a console alert when per-connection vs per-api-key accounting diverge by >5% over a 5m window.
follow_up_items: 1) Add telemetry that exposes per-route accounting deltas to Console (SRE ticket). 2) Coordinate with Dedicated onboarding to flag customers using corp-proxies and recommend proxy settings. 3) Add a KB article explaining HTTP/2 connection pooling implications for rate-limiting.
